title: Occupancy-driven page consolidation and soft-reserve allocator for paged attention cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: paged attention introduces fragmentation and small partly-filled pages in the KV cache that increase GPU memory pressure, cause more frequent remote fetches, and force suboptimal kernel selections. Existing eviction is largely age-based and does not consider page occupancy or contiguous slot availability, so decode/prefill scheduling suffers from repeated re-population of nearby slots (thrashing) and increased p99 latency during bursts.

Goal: implement an occupancy-driven consolidation pass and a soft-reserve allocation strategy to reduce fragmentation and eviction churn while preserving low-latency prefill/decode. The feature includes a background compactor that merges low-occupancy neighboring fragments into reusable pages, a soft-reserve mechanism that pins a small contiguous run of slots for hot prefixes during prefill bursts, and an eviction scoring function that combines last-access, occupancy_ratio, and compactability_score to prefer reclaiming pages that are both cold and expensive-to-keep fragmented.

Scope: kernel-selection annotations for pages (fp16-friendly / int8-optimized), allocator changes (soft-reserve window, contiguous allocation hint), background compaction scheduler (low-priority, GPU-aware), eviction policy update, metrics & exposes (compactable_pages, reserve_hits, compaction_cpu_ms), and a rollout plan for staged verification on Dedicated pools and then hosted API.

Non-goals: full online defragmentation under peak load (will defer to incremental background compaction), rewriting model kernels for custom attention; we instead tag pages so the existing kernel selector can prefer the most compatible kernels without expensive migration during hot decode paths.
acceptance_criteria: Background compaction merges adjacent low-occupancy fragments and frees at least 15% of fragmented slots on average in bursty workloads (measured on benchmark set A)
Soft-reserve allocator reduces remote fetches during 95th percentile burst by >= 12% compared to baseline on 8k sequence workloads
Eviction scoring prevents thrashing: newly compacted pages must not be evicted within 30s unless memory pressure exceeds 95% of pool capacity
No regression in median decode latency; p95/p99 decode latency improves or stays within 5% of baseline in nightly benchmarks
Metrics are emitted and dashboards created: runtime.compactor.* runtime.allocator.reserve_hits runtime.eviction.score_histogram

comments: 2025-02-18 Aisha: Created ticket after spike analysis showing 22% of pages are <25% occupied during peak. Initial design doc linked.
2025-02-20 Marco: Prototype allocator added contiguous hint in-memory structures. Observed reduce in remote fetches on synthetic workload (8%). Need compactor to reclaim fragmented pages proactively.
2025-02-24 Priya: WIP compactor scheduler. Running low-priority compaction during <40% GPU utilization windows. CPU overhead measured ~18ms per compaction cycle per GPU; acceptable so far.

2025-02-26 Evan: Implemented eviction score: score = alpha*age + beta*(1-occupancy_ratio) + gamma*fragmentation_penalty. Tuned weights to prefer reclaiming pages with low occupancy and high fragmentation.

2025-02-28 Marco: Added soft-reserve: on prefill start reserve N contiguous slots when contiguous region available. Fall back to scatter allocation if contiguous not available. Observed 14% reduction in p99 remote fetches in dedicated test cluster.
2025-03-01 Aisha: Design review comments from ML infra: ensure compactor respects per-customer isolation (do not merge pages across customer shards). Added per-shard compaction boundary checks.

2025-03-02 QA: Nightly benchmark results: median decode unchanged, p95 improved 6%, p99 improved 9% on long-context chat workload. CPU compaction cost did not push host CPU above alert thresholds in staged cluster.
2025-03-03 Marco: Opened PR #4278 with allocator and eviction changes. Requesting review from Evan and Priya. Planning canary rollout next week to two dedicated pools.
